newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Imperio buys warehouse from Danzas.
newsitem.headline: Greek Imperio buys warehouse from Danzas.

text.p: Greek forwarding agent Imperio said it bought an area of 48 acres including a warehouse and an office complex of 1,200 square metres from Swiss multinational transport company Danzas for 360 million drachmas.

"The acquisition is part of our strategy to expand in new, promising markets in the Balkans, other Eastern European and Baltic countries by setting a foothold in Thessaloniki, Northern Greece," its managing director, Christos Christolenis, told Reuters.
The warehouse, one of the most modern facilities in Greece, covers 3,000 square metres and can be expanded to 20,000 square metres, he said.

The firm went public in July 1996 by issuing 286,400 common registered shares at 1,900 drachmas each and is listed on the Athens bourse's parallel market. It closed at 2,535 drachmas on Thursday, up five drachmas.
"The cost of the investment which was 360 million drachmas accounts for 69 percent of our IPO proceeds," said Christolenis.
The Imperio Logistics Services Centre of Salonica is located in the industrial zone of Sindou and has immediate access to the most important road and rail links in Northern Greece, he said.

"I strongly believe that high rates of growth will succeed the recession some of these countries experience today, particularly in the Balkans,and I would like Imperio to be there," said Christolenis.
Imperio is one of the few Greek companies specialising in logistics and wants to build on its existing comparative advantage, he added.
The firm will announce its pre-tax profit and dividend for fiscal 1996 before the end of April, said Christolenis.
"They will be in line with forecasts in our IPO prospectus," he added.
Press reports put 1996 pre-tax profits at 600 million drachmas against 485 million in 1995. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
